mcq.question: In the podcast mirror, which tool handles which stage?

options.A: Threads download, processes hash, asyncio compresses
options.D: Asyncio for network downloads, a thread pool for disk hashing, a process pool for CPU-heavy compression

mcq.explanation: Match the tool to the bottleneck: waiting on sockets (asyncio), blocking file I/O (threads), pure CPU work (processes).

mcq.question: Why does `download_one` write to a `.part` file and rename it at the end?

options.B: So a failed or interrupted download never leaves a file that looks complete

mcq.explanation: It is the same atomic-write idea as Day 41: only finished downloads get the real name.

bonus.question: Why does the process pool use the `spawn` start method instead of `fork`? What can go wrong when forking a process that is already running threads?
Add checksum verification test-first: given a manifest of expected SHA-256 values, the mirror reports any episode whose hash doesn't match.
